author: TEDx Talks
description:
How do body image pressures affect female athletes, their performance, and their wellbeing? In this powerful TEDx talk, Dr Dominique Condo — sports nutritionist and senior lecturer at Deakin University in Melbourne, Australia — explores the hidden impact of body image in sport and why so many women still feel judged more for how they look than what they can achieve.

Drawing on years of experience working with elite athletes, Dr Condo reveals how language, culture, and expectations can shape confidence, health, and performance. She shares research-backed insights and practical strategies to create supportive environments where female performance is valued over appearance.

This talk goes beyond sport — offering lessons for workplaces, schools, and families. When we prioritise appearance over ability, we hold people back. Dr Condo challenges us to rethink how we define female performance: not by size or shape, but by strength, resilience, and capability.

Watch now and join the movemen
title: Why your body shape doesn't define athletic abilities | Dominique Condo | TEDxDeakin Uni Melbourne

author: TEDx Talks
description: Jerome poses a complex and essential question: How do you disrupt the notion of rehabilitation? By embracing his roles as a father, advocate, and husband, Jerome reminds us that joy is not seasonal is lived through service—and that each of us, within our own capacities, holds the power to care for and uplift our children, families, friends, and communities to provide more choices rather than chances.  Jerome R. Wright is a distinguished human rights activist and tireless advocate for criminal justice reform. As Co-Director of the HALT Solitary Campaign and the NYS Jails Justice Network, he works to end the use of solitary confinement and promote humane, restorative approaches within the justice system. He is also the founder and co-creator of the MAN (Mentoring and Nurturing) Program, dedicated to supporting and empowering individuals impacted by incarceration. Beyond advocacy, Jerome hosts The Wright Report on Think Twice Radio, an edutainment podcast that amplifies community voices
title: Our ability is within our capacity | Jerome R.Wright | TEDxRochester

description: Fourth-year medical students Anthony and Jack share how the bi-directional experience of caring for individuals impacted by the criminal legal system transformed their medical education, inspired the creation of a student-run free clinic, and deepened their understanding of the true essence of medicine. Jack Armstrong Bookbinder is a 4th year medical student at the University of Rochester School of Medicine and Dentistry. He grew up in Cazenovia, New York and attended Cornell University for undergraduate studies. During medical school, he has focused heavily on health equity for people involved with the criminal-legal system. This commitment began with his volunteer work providing health-related education within the Monroe County Jail. Inspired by this work, he co-founded and currently serves as Clinic Director for a student-run clinic dedicated to serving formerly incarcerated individuals in the greater Rochester community. After medical school, Jack plans to pursue a dual residency
title: Listening teaches medicine | Jack Armstrong Bookbinder & Anthony James Pamatmat | TEDxRochester

Her work bridges healthcare, research systems, and community impact, fostering meaningful connections to improve public health. A graduate of Cornell University and the Simon Business School, Laura holds a Master of Business Administration and is a registered dietitian. Outside of her professional endeavors, she is passionate about teaching yoga and cultivating a vibrant fruit and vegetable garden alongside her family. author: TEDx Talks
description:
The disability of deafness offers a path to connection resilience, and academic exploration Gaelen McCormick was a member of the Rochester Philharmonic’s double bass section from 1995-2017. Shortly after finishing her graduate degree in 2004, she was diagnosed with Meniere’s disease. The next 10+ years were an ever-changing landscape of hearing loss, distortion, vertigo, and unpredictable balance while still pursuing a career onstage. The stress associated with trying to hide the hearing loss in a VERY hearing-oriented occupation led Gaelen to search for alternative careers and alternative ways to deal with anxiety.
 
Since losing her hearing in 2017, Gaelen has forged a new career path as a composer, arranger, executive director of a chamber music festival and now is the Director for Eastman Performing Arts Medicine Center at the University of Rochester. She continues to teach the double bass through the Eastman Community Music School, educates pre-professional musicians through the
title: Hearing Silence | Gaelen McCormick, MFA | TEDxRochester

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What does it mean to truly be seen?

From growing up in foster care as “Baby Boy” to serving in the U.S. Marine Corps and building technology on Wall Street, this talk traces a personal journey toward redefining how society measures worth. Through lived experience, Brent Chandler exposes how traditional financial systems—especially credit scores—erase the full story of capable, responsible people and perpetuate exclusion from homeownership, one of the most powerful engines of generational wealth.

Blending data science, finance, and human values, the talk makes a compelling case for cash-flow–based underwriting and alternative financial data as tools for equity. It shows how technology, when designed with intention, can help institutions finally see people as they are—not as a three-digit number. Brent Chandler is founder and CEO of FormFree. He is a widely recognized innovator in mortgage and financial services technologies who has 25 years’ experience on the leading edge of trading,
title: The Theory of Being Seen: How Data Can Restore Dignity and Access | Brent Chandler | TEDxBoston

description:
A reflective talk about the nation's educational progress post the global pandemic with practical reflections about the path ahead. Dr. Christina Grant is the Executive Director of the Center for Education Policy Research at Harvard University. Throughout her career as an educator, administrator, and executive in some of America’s largest school systems, Dr. Grant has focused on data-driven leadership and strategic management to improve student outcomes and drive academic acceleration.

At CEPR, Dr. Grant unites researchers, practitioners, and policymakers to build transformative partnerships that are grounded in rigorous research, benefiting learners at every stage of life. Her leadership emphasizes the importance of evidence-based solutions in shaping effective educational policies.

Previously, Dr. Grant served as the District of Columbia’s State Superintendent of Education, where she oversaw grants, standards, assessments, and accountability for the District’s elementary and secon
title: Are The Children Well? | Christina Grant | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: Everyone is talking about Artificial Intelligence, its breakthroughs, its dangers, its potential. But beneath the headlines, there’s one crucial element almost no one is addressing… and without it, AI will fail us. In this talk, Disleve Kanku reveals the “missing ingredient” that can transform AI from a cold, mechanical force into a tool that elevates human connection, creativity, and trust. Through personal stories and real-world examples, he shows how we can design AI that serves humanity, not the other way around. Disleve Kanku is a Boston-based Data engineer and AI founder dedicated to building technology that enhances human connection. As Co-founder and CTO of echolabs, he’s developing AI-powered music intelligence to transform live experiences. At Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, he works at the intersection of AI and healthcare, creating tools that improve research and patient outcomes. His mission is to build AI systems that are as compassionate as they are intelligent. This talk
title: The Missing Ingredient in AI No One Is Talking About | Disleve Kanku | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Cotton carries a complicated history—one rooted in exploitation, loss, and forced labor. But for Troy Bridgeforth, it also carries a story of choice, resilience, and reclamation.

In this talk, Bridgeforth traces his family’s journey across five generations of cotton farming, beginning with post–Emancipation land ownership and continuing into a modern, technology-driven agricultural enterprise. He challenges the idea that legacy is something we inherit passively, arguing instead that it is something we actively shape through stewardship, education, and intention.

By reframing farming as both an economic and moral act, this talk invites audiences to rethink land ownership, conscious consumption, and the role of innovation in building equity. Bridgeforth shows how reclaiming control over land and production is not about revisiting the past, but about designing a future rooted in dignity, opportunity, and generational sustainability. Troy Bridgeforth is a fifth-generation cotton farmer,
title: From Cotton Fields to Choice: Reclaiming Land and Legacy | Troy Bridgeforth | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Healing is not abstract—it is personal, collective, and deeply necessary.

Drawing from her memoir How We Heal and her leadership in advancing racial equity, LaJune Montgomery Tabron explores what it truly takes to repair the divisions that shape American life. Through stories of racial healing circles, shared fate, and moral courage, she shows that confronting painful truths is not an act of blame, but of connection.

This talk reframes racial healing as a participatory process—one grounded in empathy, honest dialogue, and the belief that our futures are bound together. With reflections inspired by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., the principle of Ubuntu, and the wisdom of children, the talk offers a hopeful yet demanding vision: a future where healing is not optional, but essential to building a society in which all children can thrive. LaJune Montgomery Tabron is President and CEO of the W.K. Kellogg Foundation in Battle Creek, Michigan, one of the largest private foundations in the Uni
title: Ubuntu: The Work of Racial Healing | LaJune Montgomery Tabron | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Curiosity is powerful—but perseverance is what turns curiosity into impact.

In this talk, inventor and engineer Lonnie Johnson traces an extraordinary journey that spans nuclear engineering, deep-space missions, breakthrough consumer inventions, and clean energy innovation. From safeguarding spacecraft at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory to inventing the Super Soaker and pioneering next-generation energy systems, Johnson shows that innovation is rarely about sudden genius and almost always about sustained effort.

Through stories of failure, iteration, and problem-solving across science, engineering, and entrepreneurship, this talk reframes invention as an act of persistence. It is a reminder that the most transformative ideas come not from avoiding obstacles, but from working through them—with curiosity intact and purpose unwavering. Lonnie Johnson is an engineer, inventor, and entrepreneur best known as the inventor of the Super Soaker, one of the bestselling toys of all time, gene
title: How Curiosity Becomes Impact | Lonnie Johnson | TEDxBoston

In a world consumed by productivity and performance, Sian Flanagan invites us to rediscover the forgotten art of being. Through a fusion of spoken word, sound, and visual storytelling, she guides audiences on a journey from the head to the heart awakening presence, creativity, and connection. Both poetic and practical, this RantAJAM Conscious Entertainment experience challenges our modern obsession with doing and thinking, reminding us that the future of conscious leadership, humanity, and innovation begins with being and feeling.
 Sian Flanagan is the Founder of The Business of You Coaching and RantAJAM Conscious Entertainment. She is a Transformational Speaker, Poet, Embodied Leadership Coach, Award-Winning Director, Best-Selling Author, and Performance Artist passionate about helping others live vibrantly in life, body, and business. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Artificial intelligence is often framed as a threat—but what if it’s an invitation?

In this talk, comedian, creator, and cultural technologist Willonius Hatcher shares how curiosity, experimentation, and bold action led him to create BBL Drizzy—a viral AI-generated song that reshaped conversations around music, authorship, and creativity. What began as playful exploration became the first AI-sampled song to be officially credited in mainstream music history.

Hatcher reframes AI not as a shortcut or replacement for human creativity, but as a powerful amplifier of lived experience, skill, and imagination. Through humor and hard-earned insight, he challenges audiences to stop overthinking, start doing, and apply their intelligence to the most transformative tool of our time. Willonius Hatcher—also known online as King Willonius and Avocado Papi—is a comedian, creator, and cultural innovator exploring the intersection of AI, humor, and creativity. He rose to global attention after creat
title: From Curiosity to Culture: Creating With AI Instead of Fearing It | Willonius Hatcher | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“Don’t use your birthdate in your password.” You’ve heard the advice - but Anna Györgyi shows why security threats go far beyond weak passwords. In a world where money, infrastructure, and even national power systems are controlled by software, attackers often don’t “hack” machines first - they hack people, using social engineering and spear-phishing to gain access through everyday mistakes.

Drawing on real examples, from attacks on critical infrastructure to offline vulnerabilities like universal keys and easily clonable access tags, Anna reveals how security is often built through human trial-and-error… and how the same errors can be exploited. Her message is simple and urgent: the first line of defense isn’t the firewall. It’s you. Anna Györgi sheds light on the often-overlooked realities of corporate security, blending real-life stories with critical insights into both cyber and physical protection. Her talk challenges common misconceptions and invites the audience to rethink how
title: From backdoors to your front door - a talk about security | Anna Györgyi | TEDxBME

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do some ideas linger for years… while others vanish the moment a presentation ends? Public speaking coach Alex Macintosh argues that the problem isn’t your message - it’s how the brain receives it. In this talk, he introduces three “mental Post-it notes” that make ideas stick: Gloomy Glue (our negativity bias), Opening & Closing Windows (why beginnings and endings matter most), and Working Brain Drain (how cognitive overload makes people tune out).

Through stories ranging from everyday feedback to high-stakes real-world failures, Alex shows how to frame problems so people care, structure your message so they remember, and simplify so they can actually act. If you want your next pitch, lecture, or TEDx talk to land - and stay - this is your toolkit. Alex Macintosh helps professionals transform good ideas into unforgettable ones through science-backed storytelling and communication techniques. His talk uncovers why even the best ideas often fail to resonate—and offers practical too
title: Presentific: The Science Behind Sticky Ideas | Alex MacIntosh | TEDxBME

author: TEDx Talks
description: I once believed silence was safety—until the silence around me began to burn. In this talk, I share how being surrounded by quiet hurt more than any word. From schoolyards to politics, silence often shields the powerful and abandons the vulnerable. But silence doesn’t keep you safe; it keeps you small. If we want change, we must break our silence. If we do nothing, nothing changes—that silence becomes a choice with consequences. That silence is complicit. That silence isn’t neutral. title: Silence isn't Neutral: When You Say Nothing, You Say Something | Liraya Rebello | TEDxSGBIS Youth

description: Look around you. Our world, our planet, is changing. And much of that change, unfortunately, is driven by how we move around - how we connect on a day-to-day basis. For over a century, the internal combustion engine has been the king of the road. But this reign, as we all know, comes with a heavy price. The Electric Vehicle, also known as the EV is often hailed as the ultimate solution. On the surface: zero tailpipe emissions, a cleaner future. However, my research, and the core of my thesis, asks a critical question: are there better environmental solutions than electric cars? description: Innovation alone isn’t enough. Without regulation to control it, bodies turn into profiles, and profiles turn into decisions. Most of these are made without us in the room, making awareness the first line of defense. Sonika Pilli is an extraordinary young leader, artist, and changemaker—the founder of MedTeens, a pioneering platform empowering teenagers to explore healthcare careers through early awareness and mentorship. We talk about innovation, technology, and the future — but what if the real change starts within us?
In this powerful TEDx talk, Harsh Kurki reveals how self-innovation, mindset shifts, and Indian values can unlock personal growth, leadership, and nation-building, shaping a stronger and more conscious India. Harsh Vardhan Singh Kurki is an entrepreneur, consultant, and hospitality leader who bridges rich heritage with a global outlook. A 23rd-generation descendant of Meera Bai from the Rathore Rajput lineage of Kurki, he was educated at Mayo College Ajmer, Stanford Lake College (South Africa), and the University of St Andrews, Scotland. His career spans humanitarian work with UNHCR Thailand and consulting at Grant Thornton Bharat LLP. Today, as Partner at Kurki Hospitality LLP, he leads heritage hotels, restaurants, and mining ventures, while advising global investors as a GLG Council Member across emerging Indian markets. description: What if the rules that made you a top student are the same ones making you an unhappy adult? Many of us are still playing by a classroom syllabus that doesn't exist in the real world. Here, the speaker talks about 7 mindset shifts needed to break free from the perfect-student trap and navigate the chaos of life with authentic bliss. Aradhya Vats is a dynamic young leader, educator, writer, and wellness advocate, currently serving as CEO of EduAbroad. At 28, she is a triple Gold Medallist from IIM Indore, reflecting exceptional academic excellence. A certified Yoga trainer, she teaches corporates and students, fostering balance and resilience. Aradhya is also a national-level debater, published author, and researcher in management and mental health. Celebrated for blending entrepreneurship with yoga and scholarship with storytelling, she champions self-awareness as the foundation of conscious leadership and meaningful progress. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conferen

description: In this talk, Hansa examines how multitasking has evolved from a skill into an identity — especially for women. Through personal reflection, she explores burnout, guilt, and societal expectations across careers, homes, and relationships, and why redefining success has become necessary. Hansa Singla Kaicker is a creative powerhouse and a compelling voice for modern working women. She leads Retail & Design at Mac Bruzaai, is the Dreamweaver behind Events by PixieDust, and the creative force of Quirk Style Story. Spanning luxury retail, events, and décor, she balances high-impact careers with motherhood and personal wellbeing. Known for wit, authenticity, and clarity, Hansa champions conscious balance—reminding women to choose their energy as wisely as their ambitions.
